questionText: How does the word PRESENT differ in the sentence I will present the award vs She received a present?
options: C) Different stress: PRE-sent vs pre-SENT
explanation: PRESENT is a heteronym. As a verb meaning to give formally it is stressed on the second syllable: pre-SENT. As a noun meaning a gift it is stressed on the first: PRE-sent.

questionText: In which sentence is CONTENT a noun?
options: A) She was content with her results
B) The content of the book was interesting
C) He felt content after eating
D) They seem content in their work
explanation: Content as a noun (CON-tent) means what is inside or the subject matter. As an adjective (con-TENT) it means satisfied. Option B uses it as a noun.

questionText: How does the word RECORD differ in The athlete broke the record vs Please record this event?
options: B) Stress changes: REC-ord vs re-CORD
explanation: RECORD is a heteronym. As a noun (REC-ord) it means a best performance. As a verb (re-CORD) it means to register sound or video.

questionText: Which word is a homograph for BEAR (the animal)?
explanation: BEAR is a homograph - the large animal and the verb meaning to endure or carry are both spelled BEAR. They have the same spelling but different meanings.

questionText: In The wounded soldier was wound in bandages what type of word is WOUND?
explanation: WOUND is a heteronym. Wound meaning an injury is pronounced WOOND. Wound meaning wrapped (past tense of wind) is pronounced WOWND. Same spelling different pronunciation.

questionText: How does PERMIT change between Give me a permit and Will you permit me?
options: B) Stress shifts: PER-mit vs per-MIT
explanation: PERMIT is a heteronym. As a noun (PER-mit) it means an official document. As a verb (per-MIT) it means to allow.

questionText: Which sentence uses MINUTE as a heteronym meaning very small?
options: B) The minute details were overlooked
C) He arrived in a minute
D) The minute hand pointed to twelve
explanation: MINUTE meaning very small is pronounced my-NYOOT. MINUTE meaning 60 seconds is MIN-it. Option B uses the adjective form meaning extremely tiny.

questionText: How does the word OBJECT change in This is an object of beauty vs I object to that rule?
explanation: OBJECT is a heteronym. As a noun (OB-ject) it means a thing. As a verb (ob-JECT) it means to express opposition.

questionText: Which is a homograph pair?
options: A) Bow (front of ship) and Bow (weapon for arrows)
explanation: BOW is a homograph - the front of a ship (rhymes with cow) and the weapon for arrows (rhymes with low) are spelled the same. The others are homophones.

questionText: In They conduct thorough research vs She will conduct the orchestra what shifts in CONDUCT?
explanation: CONDUCT is a heteronym. As a noun (CON-duct) it means behavior or a way of doing something. As a verb (con-DUCT) it means to lead or manage.

questionText: Which sentence uses TEAR as a heteronym meaning to pull apart?
options: A) A tear rolled down her cheek
B) She had to tear the paper
C) His eyes filled with tears
explanation: TEAR meaning to rip is pronounced TARE. TEAR meaning a drop from the eye is pronounced TEER. Option B uses the verb meaning to pull apart.

questionText: How does DESERT differ in The Sahara is a desert vs He will desert his post?
explanation: DESERT is a heteronym. As a noun (DEZ-ert) it means an arid land. As a verb (de-ZERT) it means to abandon.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning both the animal and to mimic?
explanation: APE is a homograph. It means a primate animal and also to imitate or mimic someone mockingly. Same spelling same pronunciation different meaning.

questionText: In The protest was peaceful vs They protest loudly what changes?
explanation: PROTEST is a heteronym. As a noun (PRO-test) it means a statement of objection. As a verb (pro-TEST) it means to express strong objection.

questionText: Which sentence uses WIND as a heteronym meaning to turn or coil?
options: B) She will wind the thread
D) The wind knocked over the tree
explanation: WIND meaning to coil is pronounced WYND. WIND meaning moving air is pronounced WIND. Option B uses the verb form meaning to twist or coil.

questionText: What is a heteronym?
options: A) Words with same spelling and meaning
B) Words with same pronunciation but different meaning
C) Words with same spelling but different pronunciation and meaning
explanation: Heteronyms are words that are spelled the same but differ in pronunciation and meaning. They are a type of homograph.

questionText: How does INCLINE differ in Walk up the incline vs They incline toward agreement?
explanation: INCLINE is a heteronym. As a noun (IN-cline) it means a slope. As a verb (in-CLINE) it means to lean or have a tendency toward.

questionText: Which word is a homograph that can mean a type of tree and a light brownish-yellow color?
explanation: BIRCH is a homograph meaning a type of tree with smooth white bark and also a yellowish-white color. Same spelling same pronunciation different context.

questionText: In The company will abstract data vs She studied the abstract what changes in ABSTRACT?
explanation: ABSTRACT is a heteronym. As a noun or adjective (AB-stract) it refers to a concept or summary. As a verb (ab-STRACT) it means to extract or remove.

questionText: Which sentence uses LEAD as a heteronym referring to the metal?
options: A) She will lead the team
B) The pipes were made of lead
C) He took the lead in the race
D) The dog was on a lead
explanation: LEAD the metal is pronounced LED. LEAD meaning to guide is pronounced LEED. Option B uses the metal form.

questionText: How does COMPOUND differ in A chemical compound vs They will compound the problem?
explanation: COMPOUND is a heteronym. As a noun (COM-pound) it means a substance formed by combining elements. As a verb (com-POUND) it means to make something worse.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning both a type of music and a light touch?
explanation: TAP is a homograph meaning a light knock or touch and also a type of dance characterized by tapping the feet rhythmically.

questionText: In The suspect fled vs The police will suspect him what changes?
explanation: SUSPECT is a heteronym. As a noun (SUS-pect) it means a person thought to have committed a crime. As a verb (sus-PECT) it means to believe someone is guilty.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning to prevent and a defense structure?
explanation: FENCE is a homograph meaning a barrier built to enclose an area and also a person who deals in stolen goods. In fencing it means to fight with swords.

questionText: How does ENVELOPE differ in She sealed the envelope vs The fog will envelope the city?
options: C) Different spelling: envelope vs envelop
explanation: The noun is ENVELOPE (for mail). The verb meaning to surround is ENVELOP (no e at end). They are spelled differently but closely related.

questionText: Which sentence uses CLOSE as a heteronym meaning near?
options: B) The school is close to the park
C) She decided to close the account
D) He will close the gap
explanation: CLOSE meaning near is pronounced CLOZE. CLOSE meaning to shut is pronounced CLOHZ. Option B uses the adjective meaning nearby.

questionText: In They will attribute this to hard work vs This is a positive attribute what changes?
explanation: ATTRIBUTE is a heteronym. As a verb (at-TRIB-ute) it means to regard something as caused by. As a noun (AT-trib-ute) it means a quality or feature.

questionText: Which word is a homograph that can mean to press flat and a type of building?
explanation: LEVEL is a homograph meaning a flat surface, a floor in a building, a tool for checking horizontal surfaces, and the adjective meaning even or flat.

questionText: How does REFUSE differ in The refuse was collected vs I refuse to go?
explanation: REFUSE is a heteronym. As a noun (REF-use) it means garbage or waste material. As a verb (re-FUSE) it means to decline or say no.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning a type of punch and a tool for making holes?
explanation: PUNCH is a homograph meaning a forceful blow with the fist and also a tool for making holes in material such as paper or leather.

questionText: In The conflict was resolved vs This will conflict with plans what changes in CONFLICT?
explanation: CONFLICT is a heteronym. As a noun (CON-flict) it means a serious disagreement. As a verb (con-FLICT) it means to be incompatible with.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning to pull with effort and to attract?
explanation: PULL is a homograph meaning to exert force to draw toward oneself and also to attract or draw in customers or attention.

questionText: How does PROJECT differ in The project was completed vs She will project her voice?
explanation: PROJECT is a heteronym. As a noun (PRO-ject) it means a plan or undertaking. As a verb (pro-JECT) it means to throw forward or extend.

questionText: Which word is a homograph that means to save and a place where animals are kept?
explanation: RESERVE is a homograph meaning to keep for future use, an area of protected land, or a quality of being reserved in behavior.

questionText: In She has a perfect score vs She will perfect her technique what changes?
explanation: PERFECT is a heteronym. As an adjective (PER-fect) it means without any flaws. As a verb (per-FECT) it means to make perfect or improve.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning a sharp point and to impale?
explanation: PIN is a homograph meaning a thin pointed piece of metal and also the verb meaning to fasten with a pin or to hold firmly.

questionText: How does INCREASE differ in There was an increase in sales vs Sales will increase?
explanation: INCREASE is a heteronym. As a noun (IN-crease) it means a rise or growth. As a verb (in-CREASE) it means to make or become greater.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning to journey and a stumble?
explanation: TRIP is a homograph meaning a journey and also to stumble or catch the foot on something.

questionText: How does DISCHARGE differ in He received a discharge vs The doctor will discharge him?
explanation: DISCHARGE is a heteronym. As a noun (DIS-charge) it means an official release. As a verb (dis-CHARGE) it means to send away officially.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning a story and the bushy hair of an animal?
explanation: TAIL is a homograph meaning the rear appendage of an animal and also the verb meaning to follow someone secretly.

questionText: How does EXPORT differ in India exports tea vs The export was valuable?
explanation: EXPORT is a heteronym. As a verb (ex-PORT) it means to send goods abroad. As a noun (EX-port) it means a good sold to another country.

questionText: Which word is a homograph that can mean to rot and also garbage?
explanation: WASTE is a homograph meaning to use carelessly, materials left over, and also the verb meaning to fail to use effectively.

questionText: In The advocate spoke clearly vs She will advocate for change what changes?
explanation: ADVOCATE is a heteronym. As a noun (AD-vo-cate) it means a person who argues for a cause. As a verb (ad-vo-CATE) it means to publicly support.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning to secure a ship and a type of shelter?
explanation: MOOR is a homograph meaning to tie up a boat and also an area of open uncultivated land with heather.

questionText: How does SUBJECT differ in The subject was interesting vs They will subject him to tests?
explanation: SUBJECT is a heteronym. As a noun (SUB-ject) it means a topic or a person under authority. As a verb (sub-JECT) it means to cause to undergo.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning a container and to put in a container?
explanation: CAN is a homograph meaning a metal container, the ability to do something (modal verb), and the action of preserving food in cans.

questionText: How does TRANSPOSE differ from TRANSPORT in English?
options: A) One means to move to another place the other means to reverse order
B) They mean the same thing
C) TRANSPOSE means to carry and TRANSPORT means to exchange
explanation: TRANSPORT means to carry from one place to another. TRANSPOSE means to cause two or more things to change places or reverse order. Different prefixes create different meanings.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning a musical note and a written message?
explanation: NOTE is a homograph meaning a short written message, a musical sound of definite pitch, and also a verb meaning to notice or pay attention.

questionText: How does FREQUENT differ in They frequent the cafe vs Frequent visitors are welcome?
explanation: FREQUENT is a heteronym. As a verb (fre-QUENT) it means to visit often. As an adjective (FRE-quent) it means occurring regularly.

questionText: Which word is a homograph meaning to rule and a flat straight tool for measuring?
explanation: RULER is a homograph meaning a person who rules a country and also the measuring instrument with a straight edge.
